expect: Up to 4 marks for two developed points. Strength: official statistics from the Department for Education are large-scale, covering all schools in England and Wales, and longitudinal — allowing researchers to track attainment trends by class, gender and ethnicity over many years, as Halsey did in Origins and Destinations. This gives high reliability: the same data can be cross-checked and compared by different researchers. Weakness: official statistics are socially constructed — they reflect decisions about what to measure. League tables measure exam results but not the value a school adds to pupils' progress. A school serving a disadvantaged intake may appear less effective than one in a wealthy catchment area, when in reality it may be adding more to its pupils' development.
value: Up to 4 marks for two developed points. Strength: official statistics from the Department for Education are large-scale, covering all state schools in England, and longitudinal — allowing researchers to track attainment trends by class, gender and ethnicity over many years, as Halsey did in Origins and Destinations. This gives high reliability: the same data can be cross-checked and compared by different researchers. Weakness: official statistics are socially constructed — they reflect decisions about what to measure. League tables measure exam results but not the value a school adds to pupils' progress. A school serving a disadvantaged intake may appear less effective than one in a wealthy catchment area, when in reality it may be adding more to its pupils' development.
note: F7: the Department for Education covers England only. Welsh school statistics come from the Welsh Government.
